title: Learning Autoregressive Model in LSM-Tree based Store

problem.claim: Learning autoregressive models over time-series data stored in LSM-Tree-based pages must handle overlapping time ranges, incomplete data, out-of-order arrivals, inserted points, and updates across pages.

gap.claim: Merging and ordering all data points before applying existing learning algorithms is costly in I/O and prevents pre-computation of model learning.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes offline learning of autoregressive models locally in each page using incomplete data, followed by online aggregation of stored models across pages while accounting for inserted and updated data points.
The proposed method is deployed as a function in the open-source Apache IoTDB time-series database.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments in the system show LSMAR achieving up to an order-of-magnitude improvement in learning time cost.
The authors report that learning over 1 million data points requires approximately 10 milliseconds.

narrative_sequence.summary: Efficient database-native machine learning operators are desired to reduce I/O and computation costs.
Practical time-series data may be stored in overlapping LSM-Tree pages with incomplete, delayed, inserted, or updated points.
Merging and ordering points before learning increases I/O cost and prevents pre-computation.
The proposed approach learns autoregressive models locally offline in pages and aggregates them online across pages while accounting for data changes.
The method is included in Apache IoTDB, and the authors report substantial learning-time improvements.

source_observation.claim: The approach performs model learning locally on incomplete page data and aggregates stored models online as inserted and updated points are considered.

interpretation.claim: Separating local offline computation from online aggregation can reduce the need to repeatedly materialize and globally reorder mutable time-series data.

application.claim: Systems with page- or segment-oriented storage may consider maintaining local model state and incrementally combining it when data changes across segments.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy preserves model accuracy under all patterns of missing, delayed, inserted, or updated data.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the autoregressive model formulation or aggregation algorithm.
The abstract does not report accuracy metrics, baselines, datasets, or experimental conditions.
